routes: POST /v1/operator/threads/:id/messages (streamed text/event-stream: message, delta, step, card, notice, error, done; input and thread checked as JSON before the stream opens)

tests.db: throwaway cluster; full suite on a fresh database 482/485 (0 fail, 3 skipped) at the 2026-10-24 bench-r3 fix commit; ui-contract --strict 174/174

works: Tool loop: the model sees only the tools the member's role may call, as function tools built from the validators' JSON Schemas (dots mapped to underscores), plus operator_plan; every call goes through registry.execute with actor {agent, 'operator:<member>', member role} and the threadId

Receipts become cards stored as thread messages: needs_approval -> approval card (action id, plain summary, risk chip, args diff, roles that may approve, expiry); confirmed -> receipt (reads are not receipted); not_executed -> receipt with the reason in plain words; unknown -> receipt that says it will not be retried

Plans: operator_plan validates every step first, shows a plan card (which run now, which wait for a tap, which are refused), runs A1 steps, proposes the first step that needs a tap and holds the rest; the card is updated in place

A0: operator.autonomy.lower holds every draft and test the Operator makes for a tap (wrapping execute: a kernel action row, approved through /v1/actions/:id/decide); lowering and forgetting are exempt; raising back is a policy A2
Caps per turn: 6 model calls, 10 tool calls, 60k tokens, 8 plan steps; a cap ends the turn with a plain notice
Every model call writes a cost_line (component platform, tokens, priced from VP_LLM_OPERATOR_INR_MILLI_PER_MTOK_IN/OUT; inr 0 and detail.priced=false when unset)

Injection: tool results and uploads are wrapped in <data trust=untrusted> blocks, instruction-like text is flagged, a closing tag inside data is defused; a test with a maximally obedient fake model shows a malicious tool result cannot run an A2, invent an approve tool or smuggle actor/approval fields
Tenancy: thread, message, preference and brief queries filter by workspace_id; tested across two workspaces
brief.today: needs-a-tap (top 7 by risk), live campaigns, spend today in IST by component, wallet, open issues, audit changes since a time

Real streaming via Res.stream: frames are written as the turn runs (tested: the first card arrives while the next model call is still blocked); model text streams as deltas through llm.stream; the turn stops before its next model call when the client leaves

The workspace's brain is passed as the per-request model while it is on the curated list (VP_OPERATOR_BRAINS ids are the model names on the operator endpoint); a brain taken off the list falls back to the configured model

MA-01: the plan view and the model's tool list both use the kernel's heldForApproval with the Operator's actor, so attempt.retry_per_ladder shows and runs as a tap (plan stops there) while risk-lowering A3 verbs such as campaign.pause run at once; tested

Credentials never pass through the Operator: integration.stage_secrets is screen-only (not offered, refused directly and in plans with a pointer to the Integrations screen), so no secret reaches the model's tool args, an A0 action row, a card diff, the audit or SSE; tested at A1 and A0 (the test fails on the previous loop)

Chat secrets: every incoming message and upload goes through shared/safety redact() (digit secrets) and a credential detector (key prefixes sk-/AKIA/AIza/ghp_/xox and others, 'password: ...'/'token hai ...' pairs, high-entropy tokens of 24+ chars; UUIDs and hex hashes excluded) before it is stored, echoed, used as the thread title or sent to the model; one plain notice points to Settings → Integrations; tested

Tool selection (toolset.ts): at most 40 tools per model call — page tools (the web client sends `page`), tools the member's words point at, tools used earlier in the thread, a core read set, plus operator_plan and operator_find_tools. find_tools adds tools to the next model call of the same turn (max 4 lookups, no tool step). The role filter and SCREEN_ONLY are unchanged. Measured on the real modules for an owner: 166 tools / 80,361 schema chars per request before; 29-40 tools / 14,489-22,421 after (n=11). CAPS.llmCalls 6 -> 8, tokens unchanged at 60k

Tool results over CAPS.resultChars reach the model as a compact, valid JSON projection (compact.ts): ids, hashes, statuses, names, counts, errors and receipt fields kept at any depth; long strings shortened; arrays keep their first items plus the ids of the rest; large objects (drafts, briefs, configs) become a note carrying their own ids; a `truncated: {omitted, totalChars}` marker. Measured on real results: stack.list 21,484 -> 5,296 chars, agent.get 13,687 -> 5,149, agent.create 12,244 -> 3,750, stack.set 10,488 -> 1,974 (template.list 4,478 is under the cap and unchanged). The web still gets the full result

Page context reaches the model (open.2026-10-23.operator-page-context-not-sent): a short note, wrapped as untrusted data, names the page, the entity a /<section>/<id> path points at (by name, read through the registry with the Operator's own actor), and, for /campaigns, /agents or /audiences with no id or when the member's words name the kind, the only one when the workspace has exactly one; tested, including two campaigns (no guess) and another workspace's campaign (no leak)

Refusals name the fix: every NOT DONE with a field path reaches the model with a 'fix' read from the tool's own schema (allowed values, the fields that exist, the field's description, the tool's either-or note); plan steps carry it to the model but not onto the card. agent.create lists template ids as an enum and states templateId-or-description in its description (no oneOf: not every endpoint accepts it); audience.create states filter-or-contactIds with an example; brief.edit lists its editable fields and path forms

operator_find_tools: offered on every model call; its description and the system note say to call it when the needed tool is not offered and before saying something cannot be done; tested that a missed real tool is offered on the next call

A provider content-filter refusal (Azure 400 content_filter and similar) ends the turn with one plain 'the model provider refused this content' error, stoppedBy provider_refused, a system row, no retry and no attempt to get past the filter

NOT DONE is retry-first: with a fix (or a reason naming the correction) the model is told to correct the call and retry at once and to ask the client only for a fact no tool can give; campaign.draft names the published version id when it is sent an agent id, or says to publish first
The page note carries an agent's latest published version id, labelled ('use that as agentVersionId, never the agent id'), or says it has none yet

A CSV/TSV attached in chat is staged as a real intake upload as the member (role-checked), and the model is told its uploadId for source.map/source.commit; uploadId fields are described as UUIDs, never file names
A reply that claims a change with no successful write in the turn gets a plain correction notice at once and one repair turn (never looped)
Product default brain gpt-4.1 (decision.2026-10-24.operator-default-gpt41) when the deployment curates it; VP_OPERATOR_DEFAULT_BRAIN overrides; a workspace's own choice wins
untested: Numeric-provenance predicate, one-question-per-turn and the 'never say done before a receipt' conduct rules are prompt text only, not code predicates yet
Thread summary recompaction beyond the last 12 messages; the 24k compile budget
Delta streaming from a real provider: the fake emits each reply as one delta
Credential detector precision on real chat: tuned on synthetic strings only; a short password without a 'password:' label is not caught
A real model choosing tools from the reduced set and calling operator_find_tools on its own (only a scripted model was tested)
Whether a real endpoint enforces a 128-tool limit (not checked; no longer reachable at 40)
The four 2026-10-23 bench fixes are verified with a scripted model only; their effect on real models waits for the bench re-run
Page notes resolve agents, campaigns, audiences, contacts and calls by id; other pages give the path only

operator_find_tools: the loop recovers when a model calls it (scripted test), but real models called it 0 times in 96 runs; it is unused in practice. The loop also runs any role-allowed tool a model names even when it was not offered
Claim check precision on real replies: sentence patterns tuned on synthetic sentences only
needs_from_others: web: render cards (approval hold-to-confirm, receipt, plan) from the SSE frames and the thread GET
